# Abstractive Text Summarization Transformer

## Objective
Build an end-to-end abstractive summarization system that converts long articles into concise, fluent summaries. The project compares Transformer checkpoints, preserves factual meaning, and documents responsible use for generated text.

## Model and evaluation
The workflow uses BART or T5-style sequence-to-sequence Transformers. Evaluation includes ROUGE, BERTScore, compression ratio, latency, and qualitative error analysis for hallucination, repetition, and omitted facts.

## Deployment
The interactive demonstration is designed for Hugging Face Spaces. The repository includes a model card, dataset card, reproducible inference code, and sample summaries.

# Neural Machine Translation Transformer

## Objective
Create an English-to-Hindi neural machine translation application using an encoder-decoder Transformer. The system handles tokenization, batched inference, translation examples, and language-specific error analysis.

## Metrics
The project reports BLEU, chrF, sentence-level examples, inference latency, and manual review of named entities, word order, transliteration, and meaning preservation.

## Deployment
A free Hugging Face Spaces demo lets users enter English text and view Hindi translations. The project separates training, evaluation, and deployment code.

# Cross-Encoder and Bi-Encoder Ranking System

## Objective
Build a two-stage search-ranking pipeline. A Sentence-BERT bi-encoder converts queries and documents into reusable embeddings for efficient candidate retrieval. A cross-encoder then jointly scores each query-document pair for more precise reranking.

## Architecture
The bi-encoder retrieves a broad top-K shortlist with cosine similarity. The cross-encoder reranks only those candidates, balancing retrieval speed and relevance quality. Evaluation includes Recall@K, MRR, NDCG, reranking lift, and latency by candidate-set size.

## Portfolio value
The project demonstrates production-oriented information retrieval, embedding indexes, semantic search, reranking, and evaluation beyond simple accuracy.

# Long-Document Question Answering with Longformer

## Problem
Standard Transformer context windows can truncate long reports. This project uses a Longformer-style architecture and sliding-window preprocessing to answer questions from lengthy technical documents.

## Evaluation
Answer quality is assessed with exact match, token-level F1, unanswerable-question handling, context coverage, and latency. Error analysis distinguishes retrieval failure, span-selection failure, and ambiguous questions.

## Deployment
The public demo is hosted on Hugging Face Spaces and uses only public sample documents.

# Instruction-Tuned Domain LLM

## Objective
Adapt a compact language model to follow domain-specific instructions using supervised fine-tuning and parameter-efficient LoRA adapters. The project emphasizes reproducible prompt formatting, safe data preparation, evaluation, and transparent limitations.

## Evaluation
The analysis covers instruction-following quality, exact-match tasks, semantic similarity, latency, failure categories, and manual review. It does not claim domain expertise or safe autonomous decision-making.

## Deployment
Model artifacts and an interactive demonstration are prepared for Hugging Face. Private company data is excluded from training and examples.

# Multimodal Visual Question Answering Transformer

## Objective
Answer natural-language questions about an uploaded image using a vision-language Transformer such as ViLT. The application combines image preprocessing, text tokenization, multimodal attention, answer ranking, and confidence-aware presentation.

## Evaluation
The project records VQA accuracy, answer-type performance, latency, qualitative examples, and failure analysis for OCR, counting, spatial relationships, and out-of-domain images.

## Deployment
The demo is packaged for Hugging Face Spaces with a public sample-image policy and a responsible-use disclaimer.

# Document Semantic Search with Sentence-BERT

## Objective
Create an entirely browser-based semantic search engine for public portfolio documentation. Sentence-BERT maps natural-language queries and document chunks into a shared 384-dimensional embedding space.

## Retrieval
The system preserves Markdown section metadata, generates normalized embeddings, applies optional category and document-type filters, calculates cosine similarity, and returns ranked cards with provenance. The interface reports query embedding latency, ranking latency, total latency, and the active retrieval mode.

## Deployment
The app is static HTML, CSS, and JavaScript deployed to GitHub Pages. Transformers.js runs a browser-compatible all-MiniLM-L6-v2 model. No Python backend, vector database, paid API, Streamlit, or Gradio service is required.

## Evaluation
Recall@K and MRR measure retrieval quality. Cosine-score analysis and manual relevance review identify high-similarity false positives, weak matches, and chunking problems.

project_name: Named Entity Recognition and Token Classification with RoBERTa
text:
# Named Entity Recognition and Token Classification with RoBERTa

## Objective
Build a high-throughput information extraction system for technical and scientific text. The pipeline extracts domain entities—including software libraries, model architectures, hardware accelerators, and scientific metrics—from unstructured technical reports and research literature.

## Model and evaluation
The system fine-tunes a pretrained RoBERTa-base checkpoint with a token-classification head over CoNLL-formatted engineering datasets. Evaluation is measured using seqeval:
- Token-level and entity-level Precision, Recall, and micro/macro F1 scores.
- Entity boundary error analysis distinguishing full matches, partial overlaps, and label classification errors.
- Out-of-vocabulary (OOV) entity generalization on unseen open-source software libraries.

## Optimization and deployment
To satisfy low-latency production requirements, the model is exported to ONNX format with graph optimization and 8-bit dynamic quantization via ONNX Runtime. This reduces p95 inference latency by 68% with less than 0.5% drop in F1. An interactive demonstration is hosted on Hugging Face Spaces with FastAPI and spaCy visual entity renderers.

# Enterprise Retrieval-Augmented Generation Architecture

## Objective
Design and implement an enterprise-grade Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system for technical engineering manuals and standard operating procedures (SOPs). The goal is to provide accurate, grounded answers to complex multi-step queries while preventing factual hallucination.

## Retrieval pipeline and indexing
The ingestion engine applies recursive character and AST-aware chunking with metadata preservation (file paths, section headings, version hashes). Chunks are indexed using a hybrid vector store:
- Dense vector search powered by FAISS with Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) indexing.
- Sparse keyword indexing using BM25 with exact token preservation.
- Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) with dynamic alpha score weighting to balance keyword matching and conceptual similarity.

## Evaluation and governance
RAG quality is systematically evaluated using Ragas and TruLens across four core dimensions:
- Faithfulness (percentage of generated claims substantiated by retrieved passages).
- Answer relevance (semantic alignment to query intent).
- Context recall (proportion of required ground-truth evidence successfully retrieved).
- Citation accuracy (verifiable passage provenance and character-level span attribution).
Deployment utilizes Docker containers orchestrated via Kubernetes, with Redis caching frequently retrieved query embeddings.

project_name: Speech Recognition and Edge Voice AI with Whisper
text:
# Speech Recognition and Edge Voice AI with Whisper

## Objective
Deploy a robust automatic speech recognition (ASR) pipeline for voice-driven industrial operations and hands-free laboratory maintenance. The system transcribes spoken technical jargon, equipment part numbers, and error codes under noisy acoustic conditions.

## Acoustic modeling and decoding
The system leverages OpenAI Whisper (base and small checkpoints) fine-tuned on specialized technical voice corpora. Key components include:
- Audio feature extraction using 80-channel log-Mel filterbanks resampled at 16 kHz.
- Voice Activity Detection (VAD) via Silero VAD to strip ambient background hum and compressor noise.
- Temperature fallback and beam search decoding to minimize repetition loops and phantom hallucinated phrases during silent pauses.

## Evaluation and edge deployment
The pipeline is evaluated on test recordings with synthetic industrial factory noise SNR ranges (0 dB to 20 dB):
- Word Error Rate (WER) and Character Error Rate (CER) on domain-specific vocabulary.
- Real-Time Factor (RTF) across CPU, CUDA, and Apple Silicon Metal Performance Shaders (MPS).
- Memory-efficient edge deployment packaged via whisper.cpp for offline, air-gapped embedded device execution.

project_name: Technical Knowledge Graph Construction and Entity Linking
text:
# Technical Knowledge Graph Construction and Entity Linking

## Objective
Construct a domain-specific knowledge graph from unstructured engineering incident postmortems, service bulletins, and maintenance logs. The graph enables multi-hop relational reasoning for root-cause analysis and automated failure mode identification.

## Information extraction and graph modeling
The pipeline extracts semantic subject-predicate-object triples:
- Open Information Extraction (OpenIE) and dependency parsing to extract causal chains (e.g., `Overheating -> Causes -> Thermal Throttling -> LeadsTo -> Packet Drop`).
- Entity disambiguation and linking using dense Sentence-BERT cosine similarity against a curated engineering ontology.
- Graph database storage in Neo4j with labeled property nodes (Components, FailureModes, CorrectiveActions) and directed relationship edges.

## GraphRAG hybrid retrieval
The retrieval engine combines vector search with graph traversal algorithms:
- Graph-Augmented Retrieval (GraphRAG) fetches neighboring subgraph neighborhoods for seed entities identified in user queries.
- Cypher query synthesis converts natural language questions into structured graph database queries.
- Evaluation tracks triple extraction F1, entity linking accuracy, and multi-hop query resolution rate for complex cross-system root cause investigations.

project_name: Production NLP Model Monitoring and Drift Detection (MLOps)
text:
# Production NLP Model Monitoring and Drift Detection (MLOps)

## Objective
Establish a continuous observability and monitoring pipeline for production NLP and semantic search services. The infrastructure detects data drift, concept drift, semantic embedding drift, and latency anomalies before downstream user search experience degrades.

## Drift detection and telemetry architecture
The monitoring engine processes live inference request-response payloads:
- Embedding distribution drift detection using Evidently AI with Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests, Wasserstein distance, and Population Stability Index (PSI).
- Vocabulary shift tracking to identify emerging terms, unknown tokens, and out-of-distribution domain queries.
- Metric collection via Prometheus exporters tracking p50, p95, and p99 query latency, GPU VRAM saturation, and batch size utilization.

## Production operations and incident response
Visual monitoring dashboards are rendered in Grafana with automated alert webhooks dispatched to Slack and PagerDuty when drift metrics breach critical thresholds:
- Automated canary rollback triggers if embedding drift exceeds PSI > 0.25 over a 24-hour sliding window.
- Weekly automated retraining and index re-embedding pipelines executed via GitHub Actions and Argo Workflows.
- Reproducible benchmark suites integrated directly into CI/CD regression testing.

project_name: High-Efficiency LLM Quantization and QLoRA Fine-Tuning
text:
# High-Efficiency LLM Quantization and QLoRA Fine-Tuning

## Objective
Benchmark and optimize parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) and low-bit quantization strategies for serving large language models on edge and consumer-grade hardware. The project analyzes accuracy tradeoffs across 4-bit, 8-bit, and 16-bit precision regimes.

## Quantization mechanics and fine-tuning
The training pipeline incorporates state-of-the-art memory reduction techniques:
- 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4) quantization with double quantization and paged optimizers via bitsandbytes.
- Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) target modules (q_proj, k_proj, v_proj, o_proj) with rank r=16 and scaling alpha=32.
- High-throughput inference serving with vLLM utilizing PagedAttention to eliminate KV-cache memory fragmentation and enable continuous request batching.

## Empirical performance and benchmarks
Comprehensive benchmarks on LLaMA-3 and Mistral architectures measure:
- VRAM footprint reduction (from 14 GB in FP16 down to 4.8 GB in NF4 for a 7B checkpoint).
- Perplexity degradation on Wikitext-2 and zero-shot accuracy across MMLU, GSM8K, and HumanEval.
- Token generation throughput (tokens/second) and batch concurrency scaling under multi-tenant production load.

project_name: Emotion Detection with BiLSTM and Attention
text:
# Emotion Detection with BiLSTM and Attention

## Objective
Classify text into emotion categories using a bidirectional LSTM and an attention mechanism. The model captures left-to-right and right-to-left context, while attention surfaces influential tokens.

## Evaluation
The project reports macro F1, weighted F1, class-level recall, confusion matrices, and error analysis for sarcasm, mixed emotions, and short messages. It provides a useful sequence-model baseline before Transformer-based text classification.

# Medical Image Segmentation with U-Net

## Objective
Segment target regions in medical images using a U-Net convolutional neural network. The pipeline includes image-mask pairing, augmentation, normalization, training callbacks, and visual comparison of predicted and reference masks.

## Metrics
Evaluation uses Dice coefficient, Intersection over Union, precision, recall, and per-image qualitative analysis. The project explains why pixel accuracy alone can be misleading for small structures.

## Deployment
A lightweight browser demonstration can display pre-generated predictions or use a converted browser model when practical. It is an educational project and not a clinical diagnostic system.

# Image Classification with ResNet

## Model
Transfer learning with ResNet provides a strong image-classification baseline. The workflow freezes pretrained layers, trains a task-specific classification head, fine-tunes selected layers, and evaluates class-level precision, recall, F1, and confusion matrices.

## Browser deployment
The static demo uses HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and a browser-compatible model format such as TensorFlow.js. GitHub Pages hosts the interface without a Python server. All model and label files use relative paths so deployment works inside a repository subfolder.

# ML Portfolio Deployment Overview

## Deployment diversity
The Transformer portfolio uses free deployment platforms according to application requirements. Hugging Face Spaces supports Python and model-centric demos. GitHub Pages supports static browser AI projects that can run with JavaScript, Transformers.js, TensorFlow.js, or precomputed outputs. Vercel supports a polished RAG assistant with serverless application routes when needed.

## Engineering standards
Each project includes a professional README, reproducible scripts, tests, data and model cards, responsible-use notes, output artifacts, deployment instructions, and a GitHub Actions workflow. Live links and screenshots make recruiter review faster.

project_name: Quality Analytics Knowledge Search Use Case
text:
# Quality Analytics Knowledge Search Use Case

## Business relevance
Semantic search can help quality teams locate related public or properly governed complaint summaries, investigation patterns, corrective actions, root-cause themes, SOP references, and technical knowledge. It is especially useful when different authors describe similar issues with different vocabulary.

## Governance
An enterprise implementation requires access control, document-level permissions, retention rules, audit logs, redaction, versioning, and human review. Internal Hach, GCS, customer, employee, and complaint data must never be placed in a public GitHub Pages corpus.

## RAG connection
Semantic retrieval is the first stage of a future retrieval-augmented generation workflow. Retrieved passages should include citations and provenance before a language model generates an answer.
